subject: ela
intro: This quiz checks how well you use language effectively: combining and varying sentences for flow, keeping a consistent tone, matching formality to your audience, and choosing the word or revision that makes the strongest impression. Each question includes the full sentence or passage it asks about. Pick the single best answer.

items.answer: A) When the fire alarm rang, everyone hurried outside.
items.prompt:
Read the pair of sentences: "The fire alarm rang. Everyone hurried outside." Which revision combines them most effectively into one smooth sentence?
A) When the fire alarm rang, everyone hurried outside.
B) The fire alarm rang and the fact that it rang meant everyone then hurried outside.
C) The fire alarm rang everyone hurried outside.
D) The fire alarm rang, everyone hurried outside.

steps: The key is A. "When the fire alarm rang, everyone hurried outside" joins the two ideas in one clear sentence and shows the cause-and-effect link with the word "when."
B is wordy and padded; "the fact that it rang meant everyone then" adds extra words without adding meaning, so it is weaker than the tight version in A.
C is a run-on; it jams two complete sentences together with no punctuation or joining word.
D is a comma splice; a comma alone cannot join two complete sentences.
solution.answer: A) When the fire alarm rang, everyone hurried outside.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence: "The puppy went across the kitchen floor." The writer wants to show that the puppy moved quickly and playfully. Which word best replaces "went"?
A) scampered
B) demolished
C) traveled
D) proceeded

steps: The key is A. "Scampered" means to move quickly with light, playful steps, which matches the picture the writer wants of a fast, playful puppy.
B "demolished" means to destroy; it does not fit moving across a floor and distorts the meaning just because it sounds dramatic.
C "traveled" is neutral and does not add the quick, playful feeling the writer wants.
D "proceeded" sounds slow and formal, the opposite of quick and playful.

items.answer: A) OMG the ending totally blew my mind.
items.prompt:
Read this passage from a formal book report: "The novel follows a young sailor on a long voyage. The author builds suspense slowly and carefully. OMG the ending totally blew my mind." Which sentence breaks the formal tone of the passage?
A) OMG the ending totally blew my mind.
B) The novel follows a young sailor on a long voyage.
C) The author builds suspense slowly and carefully.
D) None of the sentences break the tone.

steps: The key is A. "OMG the ending totally blew my mind" uses slang and casual phrasing that clashes with the formal, careful tone of a book report.
B and C are written in clear, neutral, formal language that fits a book report, so they do not break the tone.
D is wrong because one sentence clearly does break the tone; accepting all of them ignores tone consistency even though each sentence is grammatically correct on its own.
solution.answer: A) OMG the ending totally blew my mind.

items.answer: A) Every sentence starts the same way and is the same short length; combining ideas helps: "When I opened the door and saw the mess, I sighed and started cleaning."
items.prompt:
Read the passage: "I opened the door. I saw the mess. I sighed. I started cleaning." Why does this passage feel choppy, and which revision improves the flow best?
A) Every sentence starts the same way and is the same short length; combining ideas helps: "When I opened the door and saw the mess, I sighed and started cleaning."
B) The sentences are too long; splitting them further helps: "I. Opened. The door. I. Saw. The mess."
C) The passage needs bigger words: "I unsealed the portal. I observed the disarray. I exhaled. I commenced sanitation."
D) The passage is fine and needs no revision because every sentence is grammatically correct.

steps: The key is A. Each sentence begins with "I" and is the same short length, which makes the writing choppy; combining the ideas into varied sentences smooths the flow while keeping the meaning.
B makes the choppiness worse by chopping the words into fragments.
C only swaps in fancier words; the sentences are still all the same length and structure, so the choppy rhythm remains and some words distort the tone.
D ignores flow; sentences can be grammatically correct yet still read as choppy because they all share the same opener and length.
solution.answer: A) Every sentence starts the same way and is the same short length; combining ideas helps: "When I opened the door and saw the mess, I sighed and started cleaning."

items.answer: A) I am writing to request your permission to start a chess club at our school.
items.prompt:
A student is emailing the school principal to request permission to start a chess club. Which sentence best matches the formality the situation calls for?
A) I am writing to request your permission to start a chess club at our school.
B) Hey, can you let me start a chess club or what?
C) Yo principal, chess club, make it happen please.
D) It would be of the utmost honor to be granted your most gracious permission for a club of chess.

steps: The key is A. It is polite and clear and fits a formal email to a principal without being stiff or unnatural.
B is too casual; "Hey" and "or what" are not appropriate for writing to a principal.
C is even more casual and uses slang like "Yo," which does not fit the audience or purpose.
D is overly stiff and exaggerated; the unnatural, flowery phrasing does not fit a simple, respectful request.
solution.answer: A) I am writing to request your permission to start a chess club at our school.

items.answer: A) Because it was raining, we canceled the picnic.
items.prompt:
Read the sentence: "We decided to cancel the picnic." The writer wants to explain that the cancellation happened because of rain, in the clearest and most concise way. Which revision is best?
A) Because it was raining, we canceled the picnic.
B) Due to the fact that it was raining at that point in time, we made the decision to cancel the picnic.
C) We decided to cancel the picnic and it was also raining at the time when we did that.
D) It was raining. We decided. We canceled. The picnic was canceled.

steps: The key is A. "Because it was raining, we canceled the picnic" states the cause clearly in the fewest words.
B is wordy and padded; "Due to the fact that" and "at that point in time" add length without adding meaning, so longer is not better here.
C is loose and weakly connected; it does not show the cause clearly and just tacks the rain on at the end.
D is choppy; breaking the idea into four short fragments hurts flow and buries the cause-and-effect link.
solution.answer: A) Because it was raining, we canceled the picnic.

items.answer: A) Replace "The sunlight plant got way taller, no joke" with "The plant in sunlight grew noticeably taller."
items.prompt:
Read this passage from a formal science report: "Our class studied how plants grow in different kinds of light. We placed one plant in sunlight and one in a dark closet. The sunlight plant got way taller, no joke. The closet plant stayed short and pale. We concluded that plants need light to grow well." The writer wants to keep a consistent formal tone. Which revision best fixes the sentence that breaks the tone?
A) Replace "The sunlight plant got way taller, no joke" with "The plant in sunlight grew noticeably taller."
B) Replace "The sunlight plant got way taller, no joke" with "The sunlight plant got SO much taller, seriously!"
C) Replace "We concluded that plants need light to grow well" with "So basically plants totally need light, duh."
D) Leave the passage as it is, since every sentence is grammatically correct.

steps: The key is A. "The plant in sunlight grew noticeably taller" reports the result in clear, formal language that matches the rest of the science report.
The sentence that breaks the tone is "The sunlight plant got way taller, no joke," because "way taller" and "no joke" are casual; A is the only choice that replaces it with formal wording.
B keeps the casual problem and adds more of it with "SO much" and "seriously," so it does not fix the tone.
C changes a sentence that was already formal and makes it casual with "basically," "totally," and "duh," which adds a tone break instead of removing one.
D ignores tone consistency; a sentence can be grammatically correct yet still clash with the formal tone of the passage.
solution.answer: A) Replace "The sunlight plant got way taller, no joke" with "The plant in sunlight grew noticeably taller."

items.answer: A) Replace "You really know your stuff and it was lit" with "Your knowledge and enthusiasm made the visit memorable."
items.prompt:
Read this draft of a thank-you note a student is sending to a guest speaker who visited class: "Thank you for coming to talk to us. Your stories about working as a marine biologist were fascinating. I never knew so much about deep-sea life before. You really know your stuff and it was lit. I hope you can visit again someday." The writer wants a warm but respectful tone throughout. Which revision best serves that purpose?
A) Replace "You really know your stuff and it was lit" with "Your knowledge and enthusiasm made the visit memorable."
B) Replace "Thank you for coming to talk to us" with "Sup, thanks for swinging by our class."
C) Replace "Your stories about working as a marine biologist were fascinating" with "Due to the fact that you are a marine biologist, your stories were of significant interest to me."
D) Leave the note unchanged, since the casual sentence makes it sound friendlier.

steps: The key is A. "You really know your stuff and it was lit" uses slang that clashes with the otherwise warm, respectful tone; "Your knowledge and enthusiasm made the visit memorable" stays warm while matching the rest of the note.
B replaces a polite opening with the casual "Sup" and "swinging by," which breaks the respectful tone instead of fixing it.
C makes a sentence stiff and wordy with "Due to the fact that" and "of significant interest," which loses the warmth the writer wants.
D is wrong because the slang sentence breaks the consistent tone; keeping it because it sounds friendly ignores that the rest of the note is respectful and the casual line clashes.
solution.answer: A) Replace "You really know your stuff and it was lit" with "Your knowledge and enthusiasm made the visit memorable."
